answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a signed web of trust: a new identity counts only after several established, mutually independent peers vouch for it, and each vouch is a public, slashable promise. To run N fakes, an attacker must first own or bribe N distinct trusted attestors, so the cost rises with every clone while rewards stay capped. A quartz badge of trust cannot be copied, the ember of reputation must be earned slowly across peers, and saffron collateral is forfeited when a ring is caught, making a large farm a guaranteed loss.
